title: Pinned Lean finite QFT algebra cross-check
question: Does the pinned Lean toolchain formally verify the exact finite algebraic identities used as inputs to the QFT route - trace cyclicity, four-factor transfer-word rotation, and real OS Gram positive semidefiniteness - without silently promoting them to a thermodynamic QFT theorem?

formal_scope.trace_cyclicity: For finite matrix indices over Complex, Matrix.trace (A * B) = Matrix.trace (B * A).
formal_scope.thermal_four_cycle: For finite matrices X,A,Y,B over Complex, cyclic rotation of X*A*Y*B to Y*B*X*A preserves the trace.
formal_scope.real_gram: For finite real index sets, the Gram matrix sum_k f(i,k)*f(j,k) is positive semidefinite.
formal_scope.transfer_scope: A typed Fin 1 fixture instantiates the exact finite transfer-word scope statements.

adversarial_review.check: Every trace and Gram theorem declares Fintype and DecidableEq index assumptions; no infinite-volume or continuum index is hidden in the formal statement.
The four-cycle theorem is proved by Matrix.trace_mul_comm on grouped factors and simplification by associativity; the order X*A*Y*B -> Y*B*X*A is checked exactly.
The Gram result is deliberately stated over Real because Matrix.PosSemidef requires an ordered scalar domain here; it is not mislabeled as a Complex physical-sector positivity theorem.
The source is LF-normalized, hash-registered, declaration-marked and checked against the pinned Lean/mathlib registry.
Primary and independent Python lanes parse the source and registry through separate implementations; the integrated lane reruns the pinned lake command.
This package reports exact proposition and registry checks only; it introduces no derived physical number or asymptotic fit.
Finite trace identities and a real Gram lemma do not construct a common OS carrier, KMS state, Hamiltonian identification, GNS representation, or mass gap.
The package remains auxiliary C6/Q3 infrastructure and supplies no heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, Sector-A closure or Pre-A closure.

lean_crosscheck.role: R338 is an exact finite algebra layer for the QFT-facing route. It validates identities used by finite OS/transfer diagnostics while leaving analytic, thermodynamic and physical gates explicit.

qft_interface.closed: Pinned Lean confirms the finite matrix trace rotations and the real Gram positive-semidefinite construction used as exact algebraic inputs to the finite OS/Q3 route.
qft_interface.open: The formal layer does not prove a common OS Hilbert-space carrier, source/volume-uniform Cauchy estimate, KMS state, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, GNS spectral gap, continuum limit, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary formal infrastructure only; no physical observable, source-complete exhaustion, heat-root incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, Sector-A closure or Pre-A closure is supplied.

next_action: Use R338 as a fixed exact-algebra prerequisite while attacking the still-open analytic bridge: a source-, volume-, cutoff- and beta-uniform estimate connecting finite OS words to the direct D/delta-D route.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing formal finite-algebra cross-check. It is not an analytic theorem, thermodynamic limit, mass-gap proof, continuum result, TECT claim closure, or Clay result.
no_overclaim: This package proves only the four declared finite Lean propositions and their registry integrity. It does not prove a QFT state, a common alpha, a Hamiltonian-to-OS theorem, a GNS mass gap, continuum removal, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or a Clay result.
